# Answer: generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **“only gray (5) six-cell components become
red (2); every other nonzero component becomes blue (1).”** It fits every
canonical demonstration because all canonical foreground cells are gray, but it
wrongly treats component color as semantically relevant.

This 12×14 grid contains three color-6 components of exactly six cells and three
color-7 components of other sizes. The intended rule recolors all 18 color-6
cells red (2). The rival recolors those same cells blue (1), so the predictions
differ at exactly 18 coordinates.

I checked the intended output by executing the selected canonical Racket
authority, not by trusting the generator's Python helper. The Racket output
matches the independent component oracle and differs from the rival. The exact
input, both outputs, all differing coordinates, recipe, and final generator hash
are retained in `checks/question-shortcut/report.json`.

**Does the proposed generator emit such cases?** Yes. This exact input was
emitted by the final source SHA
`4fecf23bd273239b3f322ec9eeba52b6e63a24a691a1e23ebb1302871a553af1`. More generally, two of every four scheduled
positions are non-gray six-cell witnesses. The final semantic gate measured 304
such witnesses in 600 draws, and the 300-lesson census found zero declared-rival
ambiguities in production order or across all 1,200 diagnostic query rotations.

This is finite evidence against the strongest declared shortcut, not a proof
that no other computable rival exists.
